sections.h2: Selling in Flagstaff: what is different
sections.html:
Flagstaff is the Coconino County seat, about 146 miles north of Phoenix at roughly 7,000 feet, inside a huge ponderosa pine forest. It has an estimated 77,260 residents as of July 1, 2025. Snow, altitude and trees affect every house here, and the Rio de Flag runs only after rain or snowmelt.

The housing mix is unusual for Arizona. Only 42.3% of housing units are owner-occupied, so more households rent than own, and 69.8% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. The median owner-occupied home is worth $552,900, median monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $1,999, median gross rent is $1,645, and the median household income is $71,512. Buyers will notice the gap between price and income, and investors as well as owner-occupants shop this market. The mean trip to work is 16.5 minutes.

Weather decides what a Flagstaff inspector looks at. Precipitation averages 21.6 inches a year, the monsoon runs July to September, and the record low is minus 30 degrees F, set in January 1937. Expect close attention to the roof, insulation, heating and drainage, with snow load and monsoon runoff in mind.

Seasonal city rules affect showings and rentals too:

  • Parking on city streets is prohibited from midnight to 7 a.m., November 1 through April 1, so plan driveway space for visitors and inspectors.
  • During Stage 2 or higher fire restrictions, owners of short-term rentals that hold a city license must remove, disable or lock fire pits and open-flame grills.
  • The city's rental rules call for exits free of snow and ice. Clear them for every winter showing, rental or not.

Time and a change of owner do not make unpermitted work legal. Flagstaff's Building Safety and Code Compliance Section says there is no statute of limitation on illegal construction. If an owner makes no progress toward a permit, a Notice and Order is recorded with the Coconino County Recorder and attaches to the property title, where any buyer's title search will find it.

To legalize work, follow these steps:

  • Call Building Safety at 928-213-2628 to meet an inspector
  • Submit a permit application and two sets of as-built plans drawn by an Arizona architect, engineer or contractor
  • Expose covered work so it can be inspected, and correct anything that fails current code
  • Pass a final inspection, which lets the city rescind any recorded Notice and Order

The city may reduce permit fees when the current owner shows that a previous owner did the work. Compare the cost and time of legalizing with selling the house as is and telling the buyer about the problem.

Every short-term rental owner in Flagstaff has needed a city Short Term Rental License since November 2023. The license lasts one year and costs $250 under the 2026 ordinance update. Applicants need an Arizona Transaction Privilege Tax license that shows the property address, and written notice to single-family neighbors who are adjacent, across the street or diagonal.

The 2026 update added requirements at renewal:

  • $500,000 of liability insurance, which a booking marketplace can satisfy
  • A sex offender registry check within 24 hours before each stay
  • Smoke alarms, carbon monoxide detectors, a fire extinguisher and clear exits
  • Owner occupancy if an accessory dwelling unit received its certificate of occupancy on or after September 14, 2024

The city reviews applications in seven business days. If your house has operated as a rental, call the Short Term Rental office at (928) 213-2231 and ask what happens to the license when the property sells.

Coconino County bills in two halves, due October 1 and March 1, and the first half turns delinquent in early November each year. Late payments carry 16% annual interest, prorated at 1.33% per month.

Primary residences are Legal Class 3, non-primary residences Class 4.1 and residential rentals Class 4.2, so tell your buyer which class your parcel carries.

The Assessor mails a Notice of Value each February and gives owners 60 days from the mail date to appeal. Read the notice the day it arrives, because the window is short. If you believe the value is too high, gather recent sales of comparable houses and file within the 60 days. Keep a copy of the notice and the date it was mailed, since the clock starts then and not when you open the envelope. A buyer who sees a recent appeal in the file will ask how it ended, and a clear answer helps the sale along. Call the Assessor if you are unsure how the process works for your parcel. Ask your escrow officer how the year's tax will be divided between you and the buyer at closing, whatever the appeal outcome.

Coconino County charges a flat $30 to record a document, and the fee covers the affidavit of property value and postage. The county adopted the flat fee on July 1, 2019, and it applies to deeds of conveyance as well as deeds of trust.

State law requires the affidavit under A.R.S. 11-1133, and A.R.S. 11-1134 exempts transfers such as gift deeds and court-ordered conveyances. Escrow takes care of both, so your part is giving the title officer accurate names and parcel details.

A Flagstaff sale moves in a predictable order. You accept an offer, and escrow opens with a title company. The title officer searches the record for liens and any recorded Notice and Order, asks your lender for a payoff figure, and splits the year's property tax. At signing you sign the deed, the buyer funds, and the deed is recorded with Coconino County.

A cash buyer removes the lender from this chain. There is no appraisal and no loan approval to wait for, so the closing date depends mostly on title work and on when you can move out. A financed buyer needs those too, and inspections tied to roof, heat and drainage can add repair requests in a snowy market.

Before you open escrow, collect your tax bill, your permit history, any HOA or rental license details, and records of recent roof and heating work. Buyers in a college and tourism town ask about rental history, so be ready to answer it plainly.

faqs.q: How many people live in Flagstaff?
faqs.a: The population is 77,260 as of July 1, 2025, up slightly from the 76,831 counted in 2020. Flagstaff is the Coconino County seat.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Flagstaff house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. Flagstaff requires a Short Term Rental License, which costs $250 a year, along with a state Transaction Privilege Tax license and written notice to nearby neighbors. The city can also issue notices if a property operates without a license.

faqs.q: Does Flagstaff have rules about unpermitted construction?
faqs.a: Yes. There is no statute of limitation on unpermitted work, and a recorded Notice and Order can attach to the property title. Call Building Safety at 928-213-2628 to start the legalization process.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Coconino County?
faqs.a: The Coconino County Recorder charges a flat $30 for most documents, including deeds. The fee includes the affidavit of property value and postage.

faqs.q: What is the winter parking rule in Flagstaff?
faqs.a: Parking on city streets is prohibited from midnight to 7 a.m., November 1 through April 1. Plan for that when you host showings or have buyers visiting for an inspection.
